title: Diagrams that change, with React Flow
description: Adds flow fences: a Mermaid flowchart drawn in the browser by React Flow and laid out by dagre, whose versions, split by lines of ---, are steps. Nodes that stay glide to their new places along redrawn edges, new ones fade in, removed ones stay as ghosts for the step, and badges mark what is new, changed, moved or removed. The diagram fits the room its slide leaves and reports a shrink below its drawn size like a Mermaid diagram; the README, the writing-slides skill and a VS Code snippet document it.

A `flow` fence is a Mermaid flowchart drawn in the browser by [React Flow](https://reactflow.dev) and laid out by [dagre](https://github.com/dagrejs/dagre), for a diagram that changes while you talk. Lines of `---` split it into versions, and each version is a step: nodes that stay move to their new places, new ones fade in, and what a version removes stays as a dashed ghost until the next, so the printed slide shows the whole change.

Only the first version needs the `flowchart` line; later ones keep its direction. A node is the same node in every version that uses its id. Shapes, edge labels and `-->`, `-.->`, `==>` and `---` edges are Mermaid's, and a class gives a node a tone: `:::primary`, `:::muted`, `:::success`, `:::warning` or `:::danger`. After the language, `direction=TB` sets the direction and `duration=800` how long each change takes, in milliseconds; a second by default.
A node a version changes carries a badge, and new edges draw in green:
| New     | is not in the version before                    |
| Changed | has a new label, shape or tone                  |
| Moved   | no longer comes from a node that is still there |
| Removed | is gone, and stays as a ghost for this step     |

The diagram fills the room its slide leaves, up to 1.25 times its size, and shrinks when the room is smaller; the slide's corner says so, since its labels then fall under 18 px. Five nodes fit in a row, and four ranks top to bottom. In VS Code, typing `flow` in a slide offers a fence to start from.
## A `flow` fence animates a diagram from one version to the next

stays as a ghost, so the printed slide shows the whole change. React Flow
draws the diagram and dagre lays it out.

content: The `flow` fence of this deck: when to use it over `mermaid`, its syntax, what its badges mean, and how much fits.

A `mermaid` fence is drawn once, when the deck builds, and suits a diagram that stays the same. A `flow` fence is drawn in the browser by React Flow, so it can change as the talk goes: use it when the change is the point, such as an architecture before and after a migration, a request path that gains a cache, or a pipeline that loses a stage. The versions go in one fence on one slide, never in a diagram per slide.
A Mermaid flowchart, with a line of `---` between versions. Each version is a step, animated from the one before, and the print view shows the last.
## A cache in front of Postgres took the search index's place
- Only the first version needs `flowchart LR`; later ones keep its direction.
- A node is the same node in every version that uses its id, so `db` above moves where a new id would fade in as a new node. Changing its label keeps the node and marks it Changed.
- Shapes are Mermaid's: `[box]`, `(rounded)`, `([stadium])`, `((circle))`, `{diamond}`, `{{hexagon}}`, `[(cylinder)]` and `[[subroutine]]`. Others are drawn as boxes, with a warning.
- Edges are `-->`, `-.->` (dotted), `==>` (thick), `---` (no arrow) and `-->|label|`, one edge per pair of nodes. Subgraphs are drawn without their frame.
- `:::primary`, `:::muted`, `:::success`, `:::warning` or `:::danger` after a node gives it a tone. `style` and `classDef` are ignored.
- After the language: `direction=TB` (or `LR`, `RL`, `BT`), and `duration=800`, how long each change takes in milliseconds, a second by default.
Each version is compared with the one before, node by node, and a node that changed carries a badge:
| New | was not in the version before |
| Changed | has a new label, shape or tone |
| Moved | no longer comes from a node that is still there |
| Removed | is gone, and stays as a dashed ghost for this step |

New edges are green and removed ones dashed red. Plan the versions so each step changes what the speaker is talking about at that moment: a step that lights up four badges is a slide the audience reads instead of listening. A node that only gains an input is not marked; its new edge shows the change.
Measured on this deck at full size, with labels at 18 px:
| Diagram | Fits at full size | One more |
| Left to right | 5 nodes in a row | 6 shrink to 92% |
| Top to bottom | 4 ranks, under a one- or two-line headline | 5 shrink to 88% or 78% |
| Several nodes into one | 4 stacked, under a two-line headline | 5 shrink to 88% |

A diagram smaller than its room grows, up to 1.25 times. Past these limits it shrinks, and `pnpm check` warns that the slide was shrunk to fit: treat that as a failure, and cut nodes, shorten labels, or split the change across two slides.
